item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Wed Sep 2 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The Weather Prediction Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Edouard, located inland over southeastern Texas.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Summary for Tropical Depression Edouard (AT5/AL052026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...EDOUARD PRODUCING SIGNIFICANT FLASH FLOODING ACROSS EAST TEXAS... As of 10:00 AM CDT Wed Sep 02 the center of Edouard was located near 31.3, -95.0 with movement NNW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1004 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 35 mph.

item.title: Tropical Depression Edouard Public Advisory Number 9
item.description: The NHC has issued its final advisory on this system. Public Advisories from the Weather Prediction Center will provide updates as long as the system remains a flood threat. Issued at 1000 AM CDT Wed Sep 02 2026

item.title: Tropical Depression Edouard Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Wed Sep 02 2026 
958 
WTNT45 KWNH 021450
TCDAT5
 
Tropical Depression Edouard Discussion Number   9
NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD   AL052026
1000 AM CDT Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php
 
For a list of rainfall observations and wind reports associated
with Edouard, see the companion storm summary at WBCSCCNS5 with the
WMO header ACUS45 KWBC or at the following link:
www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/discussions/nfdscc5.html.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph will continue near the center of
Edouard for the next several hours.
 
2. As the depression lifts slowly to the north-northwest, heavy rain 
bands from Edouard will continue pulling away from the Upper Texas 
coast and southwest Louisiana over the course of the morning, while 
slowly tracking across east-central Texas through Thursday morning. 
Flash flooding is likely across this region, especially in urban 
areas. Significant to locally catastrophic flash flooding is likely 
over the Piney Woods area of southeast Texas. River flooding may 
also be possible.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
